chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Sama'a ibn Mihran who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the edible from the birds and the wild beasts. So he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited every bird with claws and every wild beast with fangs.

So I said: The people are saying (it is prohibited) from predatory animals. So he said to me: O Sama'a! All predatory animals are forbidden, even if the predatory animal has no fangs; the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said this in detail. And God, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited all transformed creatures.

So now, eat from the birds of land those that have a crop, and from the birds of water those that have a gizzard like the gizzard of a dove — not a stomach like the stomach of a human. Every bird that soars and has claws is forbidden, and the soaring flight is like the flight of the hawk, the falcon, the kite, and whatever resembles that. Every bird that flaps its wings is permissible. The crop and gizzard are used to examine those birds whose flight pattern is unknown, and every unknown bird.

key_terms.السَّبُع: Predatory/carnivorous animals — all are forbidden regardless of specific features
key_terms.الْمُسُوخ: Transformed/morphed creatures — a category of creatures cursed and forbidden
key_terms.حَوْصَلَة: Crop/craw — an organ present in permissible land birds
key_terms.دَفَّ: To flap wings — characteristic of permissible birds
key_terms.صَفَّ: To soar/glide with outspread wings — characteristic of forbidden raptors
key_terms.قَانِصَة: Gizzard — an organ present in permissible water birds (resembling a dove's)
key_terms.مِخْلَب: Claw/talon — the defining feature distinguishing forbidden raptors from permissible birds
key_terms.نَاب: Fang/canine tooth — the defining feature of forbidden wild beasts

ai.seo_question: What are the criteria for permissible birds and wild animals to eat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a comprehensive ruling on permissible birds and wild beasts in response to Sama'a ibn Mihran's question. The hadith clarifies that the Prophet's prohibition covers all clawed birds and fanged beasts, and further that all predatory animals are forbidden regardless of whether they have fangs. A practical criterion is given: land birds with a crop (حوصلة) and water birds with a gizzard like a dove's (not a human-like stomach) are permissible, while birds that soar with claws (like hawks, falcons, and kites) are forbidden; birds that primarily flap their wings are permissible. The crop/gizzard test serves as a physical indicator for identifying unknown birds.
